_comment: Lexical (regex, comment-stripped) and structural (path) checks. No syntax-tree or route-graph checks currently exist (tried a syntax-tree check and cut it -- the lexical regex checks already cover the same ground once properly anchored; a route-graph check needs its own research pass on Metro internals, see git history). Future code-driven checks would register via @register instead of being declared here. Every check here is skill-agnostic; skill_map.json is the only file that says which skill(s) currently claim a given check.

checks.description: Uses a real expo-router navigation API -- declarative (<Link>, <Redirect>) or imperative (useRouter/useLocalSearchParams/useSegments/usePathname/useNavigation) -- all are valid per the skill, not just the <Link> tag. Verified against a real authored app that legitimately uses only useRouter().

Uses a real Stack/Tabs/NativeTabs/Drawer/Slot JSX element, not a bare word match. Drawer confirmed necessary against a real wiki_reader app using expo-router/drawer -- a Stack/Tabs/NativeTabs-only list would have false-negatived on legitimate code.
SDK 56+ rule: never import @react-navigation/* directly -- use expo-router/react-navigation instead

At least one index route exists (proxy for 'the app always has a route matching /'). Known limitation: matches any index.* anywhere under app/, not specifically the root -- an app with only a nested index (e.g. app/settings/index.tsx) and no real root route would still pass. Verified correct on 2 real apps using route groups ((tabs)/index.tsx, (drawer)/index.tsx), since groups don't affect the URL path -- but this is a proxy, not a real route-graph check (deferred, see uptake_checks/README.md).
At least one _layout file exists -- the skill's rule: ALWAYS use _layout.tsx to define stacks

Anti-pattern the skill calls out by name: never co-locate components/types/utilities in the app directory. This is a denylist heuristic, not exhaustive -- it can miss the anti-pattern under an unlisted name, and could in principle false-positive if an app has a genuine *route* literally named one of these (not observed in any real app checked so far).
Uses StyleSheet.create -- colocated-styles signal (paired with the absence check below)
components/ (or src/components/) exists for reusable UI
Anti-pattern: the skill says colocate StyleSheet.create in the component file, not a separate *.styles.ts file
Anti-pattern: the skill prefers colocated x.test.ts beside x.ts over a __tests__/ folder
